# AUGMANITAI Master Compendium — Stage-0

> The master library of the AUGMANITAI Research Programme by Andreas Ehstand:
> defined terms describing observable patterns of human-AI and human-technology
> interaction. Bilingual descriptive phenomenology (EN/DE). CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

## About

Descriptive phenomenology of patterns observed when humans interact with AI
systems and technology. One page per named pattern, bilingual EN/DE, citation-ready
with a stable canonical Concept-DOI. Independent academic research project —
descriptive, not normative; no commercial offer; AI-assisted and human-reviewed.

## Structure

- Defined terms grouped into topical clusters and thematic branches
  (AUGMANITAI · NEOMANITAI · PERMANITAI · ROBMANITAI · EDUMANITAI · JOBMANITAI)
- Atlas index: /atlas/
- Domains overview: /domains/
- Disclaimer §1–§40 (bilingual EN/DE): /disclaimer/
- Impressum (DE): /impressum/
- Datenschutz (DE): /datenschutz/

## Methodology

Descriptive phenomenology adapted from high-performance sport coaching.
Each term documents an observable pattern without prescriptive recommendation.
Inspired by ISO 704 / ISO 1087 / ISO 30042 (inspired, NOT compliance-claimed);
aligned with W3C SKOS, schema.org, and PROV-O-style provenance.

Static descriptive research artifact; not an AI system; does not interact with
users via AI. Content is AI-assisted and human-reviewed; synthetic-content
marking is machine-readable (see ai.txt and per-page meta tag).
